page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: State the logarithmic form
steps.margin_note: First mark. Every inverse hyperbolic function has a logarithmic form, and writing the right one is the mark. For Sinh⁻¹ the surd carries a PLUS one.
steps.memory_tip: For Sinh⁻¹ the surd carries a PLUS one: logₑ(x + √(x² + 1)). Cosh⁻¹ is the one with a minus.

recall.must_convey: That the logarithmic form Sinh⁻¹x = logₑ(x + √(x²+1)) is stated, with +1 under the root.
accept: sinh inverse x is log of x plus root x squared plus one
state the logarithmic form with plus one under the root
write the formula for sinh inverse
sinh inverse ki log form rasta, x plus root x square plus one
quote the log formula for sinh inverse

steps.why: Sinh⁻¹ has +1 under the root and Cosh⁻¹ has −1. Getting that sign wrong is the difference between a real answer and an impossible one.
common_mistakes: Writing √(x² − 1), which is the Cosh⁻¹ form.

steps.label: Substitute x = 3
steps.margin_note: Second mark. sinh x = 3 means x is Sinh⁻¹(3). Substitute and simplify the surd: 9 + 1 = 10.
steps.memory_tip: 9 + 1 = 10, so the answer is logₑ(3 + √10). √10 is not √9 + √1.
lines: Given sinh x = 3, so x = Sinh⁻¹(3)

recall.must_convey: That x = Sinh⁻¹(3) is substituted into the formula to give logₑ(3 + √10).
accept: x is sinh inverse three so substitute to get log of three plus root ten
nine plus one is ten so the answer is log three plus root ten
three substitute cheste log of three plus root ten vasthundi
the answer is log e of three plus root ten

steps.why: sinh x = 3 and x = Sinh⁻¹(3) say the same thing. Reading the given equation as an inverse is what lets the formula be used at all.
common_mistakes: Trying to solve the exponential definition from scratch.
